verses.1: The words of Nehemiah son of Haggai. It was in the month of Kislev, in the year 40. I was then in Shushan, the capital city.
verses.2: And one of my brothers, along with men from Judah, came to me. They asked me about the Jews who remained behind from the exile, and about Jerusalem.
verses.3: And those who remained from the exile said to me, “We have been left there in a terrible situation of suffering and disgrace. Jerusalem is in ruins, and its gates have been destroyed by fire.”
verses.4: And when I heard these words, I sat down and wept. I cried for days, and I prayed before the God of heaven.
verses.5: And He said, “I, Jehovah, the God of the heavens, the great and glorious God, who keeps His covenant and kindness for those who love Him and obey His commands.”
verses.6: May your ears be attentive, and your eyes open to hear the prayers of your servants. I pray before you today, day and night, for the children of Israel, your servants. I also weep over the sins of the children of Israel, who have sinned against you. We, along with our ancestors, have also sinned.
verses.7: We have broken the laws and commandments that you commanded Moses, your servant. We have not obeyed them.
verses.8: Remember what you commanded Moses, your servant, saying, “You shall be exalted; I will scatter you among the nations.”
verses.9: And you returned to me, and you obeyed my commands. But if you were rejected at the ends of the heavens, then I will bring you back to the place I have chosen for me to dwell in.
verses.10: And they are your servants and your people, whom you have redeemed by your great power and your strong hand.
verses.11: Oh Lord, may your ear be attentive to the prayers of your servants and those who desire to see your name glorified. May they be successful in serving you today. Please grant them mercy before this man. I am ready to serve the king.
